- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after a spike in price or sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by lowering forecast 1–3% from peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast to sentiment median rather than peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 70% of 30-day moving average, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for each negative sentiment day in sequence.
